scene.label: Act 1, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. Verona. An open place

lines.text: Cease to persuade, my loving Proteus.
lines.plainText: Cease to persuade my loving Proteus

lines.text: Home-keeping youth have ever homely wits.
lines.plainText: Homekeeping youth have ever homely wits

lines.text: Were't not affection chains thy tender days
lines.plainText: Were't not affection chains thy tender days

lines.text: To the sweet glances of thy honoured love,
lines.plainText: To the sweet glances of thy honoured love

lines.text: I rather would entreat thy company
lines.plainText: I rather would entreat thy company

lines.text: To see the wonders of the world abroad
lines.plainText: To see the wonders of the world abroad

lines.text: Than, living dully sluggardized at home,
lines.plainText: Than living dully sluggardized at home

lines.text: Wear out thy youth with shapeless idleness.
lines.plainText: Wear out thy youth with shapeless idleness

lines.text: But since thou lov'st, love still, and thrive therein,
lines.plainText: But since thou lov'st love still and thrive therein

lines.text: Even as I would when I to love begin.
lines.plainText: Even as I would when I to love begin

lines.text: Wilt thou be gone? Sweet Valentine, adieu.
lines.plainText: Wilt thou be gone Sweet Valentine adieu

lines.text: Think on thy Proteus when thou haply seest
lines.plainText: Think on thy Proteus when thou haply seest

lines.text: Some rare noteworthy object in thy travel.
lines.plainText: Some rare noteworthy object in thy travel

lines.text: Wish me partaker in thy happiness
lines.plainText: Wish me partaker in thy happiness

lines.text: When thou dost meet good hap; and in thy danger,
lines.plainText: When thou dost meet good hap and in thy danger

lines.text: If ever danger do environ thee,
lines.plainText: If ever danger do environ thee

lines.text: Commend thy grievance to my holy prayers,
lines.plainText: Commend thy grievance to my holy prayers

lines.text: For I will be thy headsman, Valentine.
lines.plainText: For I will be thy headsman Valentine

lines.text: And on a love-book pray for my success?
lines.plainText: And on a lovebook pray for my success

lines.text: Upon some book I love I'll pray for thee.
lines.plainText: Upon some book I love I'll pray for thee

lines.text: That's on some shallow story of deep love,
lines.plainText: That's on some shallow story of deep love

lines.text: How young Leander crossed the Hellespont.
lines.plainText: How young Leander crossed the Hellespont

lines.text: That's a deep story of a deeper love,
lines.plainText: That's a deep story of a deeper love

lines.text: For he was more than over shoes in love.
lines.plainText: For he was more than over shoes in love

lines.text: 'Tis true; for you are over boots in love,
lines.plainText: 'Tis true for you are over boots in love

lines.text: And yet you never swam the Hellespont.
lines.plainText: And yet you never swam the Hellespont

lines.text: Over the boots? Nay, give me not the boots.
lines.plainText: Over the boots Nay give me not the boots

lines.text: No, I will not, for it boots thee not.
lines.plainText: No I will not for it boots thee not

lines.text: What?
lines.plainText: What

lines.text: To be in love, where scorn is bought with groans,
lines.plainText: To be in love where scorn is bought with groans

lines.text: Coy looks with heart-sore sighs, one fading moment's mirth
lines.plainText: Coy looks with heartsore sighs one fading moment's mirth

lines.text: With twenty watchful, weary, tedious nights.
lines.plainText: With twenty watchful weary tedious nights

lines.text: If haply won, perhaps a hapless gain;
lines.plainText: If haply won perhaps a hapless gain

lines.text: If lost, why then a grievous labour won;
lines.plainText: If lost why then a grievous labour won

lines.text: However, but a folly bought with wit,
lines.plainText: However but a folly bought with wit

lines.text: Or else a wit by folly vanquished.
lines.plainText: Or else a wit by folly vanquished

lines.text: So, by your circumstance, you call me fool.
lines.plainText: So by your circumstance you call me fool

lines.text: So, by your circumstance, I fear you'll prove.
lines.plainText: So by your circumstance I fear you'll prove

lines.text: 'Tis love you cavil at. I am not Love.
lines.plainText: 'Tis love you cavil at I am not Love

lines.text: Love is your master, for he masters you;
lines.plainText: Love is your master for he masters you

lines.text: And he that is so yoked by a fool
lines.plainText: And he that is so yoked by a fool

lines.text: Methinks should not be chronicled for wise.
lines.plainText: Methinks should not be chronicled for wise

lines.text: Yet writers say, as in the sweetest bud
lines.plainText: Yet writers say as in the sweetest bud

lines.text: The eating canker dwells, so eating love
lines.plainText: The eating canker dwells so eating love

lines.text: Inhabits in the finest wits of all.
lines.plainText: Inhabits in the finest wits of all

lines.text: And writers say, as the most forward bud
lines.plainText: And writers say as the most forward bud

lines.text: Is eaten by the canker ere it blow,
lines.plainText: Is eaten by the canker ere it blow

lines.text: Even so by love the young and tender wit
lines.plainText: Even so by love the young and tender wit

lines.text: Is turned to folly, blasting in the bud,
lines.plainText: Is turned to folly blasting in the bud

lines.text: Losing his verdure even in the prime,
lines.plainText: Losing his verdure even in the prime

lines.text: And all the fair effects of future hopes.
lines.plainText: And all the fair effects of future hopes

lines.text: But wherefore waste I time to counsel thee
lines.plainText: But wherefore waste I time to counsel thee

lines.text: That art a votary to fond desire?
lines.plainText: That art a votary to fond desire

lines.text: Once more adieu. My father at the road
lines.plainText: Once more adieu My father at the road

lines.text: Expects my coming, there to see me shipped.
lines.plainText: Expects my coming there to see me shipped

lines.text: And thither will I bring thee, Valentine.
lines.plainText: And thither will I bring thee Valentine

lines.text: Sweet Proteus, no. Now let us take our leave.
lines.plainText: Sweet Proteus no Now let us take our leave

lines.text: To Milan let me hear from thee by letters
lines.plainText: To Milan let me hear from thee by letters

lines.text: Of thy success in love, and what news else
lines.plainText: Of thy success in love and what news else

lines.text: Betideth here in absence of thy friend;
lines.plainText: Betideth here in absence of thy friend

lines.text: And I likewise will visit thee with mine.
lines.plainText: And I likewise will visit thee with mine

lines.text: All happiness bechance to thee in Milan.
lines.plainText: All happiness bechance to thee in Milan

lines.text: As much to you at home, and so farewell.
lines.plainText: As much to you at home and so farewell

lines.text: He after honour hunts, I after love.
lines.plainText: He after honour hunts I after love

lines.text: He leaves his friends to dignify them more;
lines.plainText: He leaves his friends to dignify them more

lines.text: I leave myself, my friends, and all for love.
lines.plainText: I leave myself my friends and all for love

lines.text: Thou, Julia, thou hast metamorphosed me,
lines.plainText: Thou Julia thou hast metamorphosed me

lines.text: Made me neglect my studies, lose my time,
lines.plainText: Made me neglect my studies lose my time

lines.text: War with good counsel, set the world at nought;
lines.plainText: War with good counsel set the world at nought

lines.text: Made wit with musing weak, heart sick with thought.
lines.plainText: Made wit with musing weak heart sick with thought

lines.text: Sir Proteus, 'save you. Saw you my master?
lines.plainText: Sir Proteus 'save you Saw you my master

lines.text: But now he parted hence to embark for Milan.
lines.plainText: But now he parted hence to embark for Milan

lines.text: Twenty to one, then, he is shipped already,
lines.plainText: Twenty to one then he is shipped already

lines.text: And I have played the sheep in losing him.
lines.plainText: And I have played the sheep in losing him

lines.text: Indeed a sheep doth very often stray,
lines.plainText: Indeed a sheep doth very often stray

lines.text: An if the shepherd be a while away.
lines.plainText: An if the shepherd be a while away

lines.text: You conclude that my master is a shepherd then, and I a sheep?
lines.plainText: You conclude that my master is a shepherd then and I a sheep

lines.text: I do.
lines.plainText: I do

lines.text: Why then, my horns are his horns, whether I wake or sleep.
lines.plainText: Why then my horns are his horns whether I wake or sleep

lines.text: A silly answer, and fitting well a sheep.
lines.plainText: A silly answer and fitting well a sheep

lines.text: This proves me still a sheep.
lines.plainText: This proves me still a sheep

lines.text: True, and thy master a shepherd.
lines.plainText: True and thy master a shepherd

lines.text: Nay, that I can deny by a circumstance.
lines.plainText: Nay that I can deny by a circumstance

lines.text: It shall go hard but I'll prove it by another.
lines.plainText: It shall go hard but I'll prove it by another

lines.text: The shepherd seeks the sheep, and not the sheep the shepherd; but I seek my master, and my master seeks not me. Therefore I am no sheep.
lines.plainText: The shepherd seeks the sheep and not the sheep the shepherd but I seek my master and my master seeks not me Therefore I am no sheep

lines.text: The sheep for fodder follow the shepherd; the shepherd for food follows not the sheep. Thou for wages followest thy master; thy master for wages follows not thee. Therefore thou art a sheep.
lines.plainText: The sheep for fodder follow the shepherd the shepherd for food follows not the sheep Thou for wages followest thy master thy master for wages follows not thee Therefore thou art a sheep

lines.text: Such another proof will make me cry "baa".
lines.plainText: Such another proof will make me cry baa

lines.text: But dost thou hear? Gav'st thou my letter to Julia?
lines.plainText: But dost thou hear Gav'st thou my letter to Julia

lines.text: Ay, sir. I, a lost mutton, gave your letter to her, a laced mutton, and she, a laced mutton, gave me, a lost mutton, nothing for my labour.
lines.plainText: Ay sir I a lost mutton gave your letter to her a laced mutton and she a laced mutton gave me a lost mutton nothing for my labour

lines.text: Here's too small a pasture for such store of muttons.
lines.plainText: Here's too small a pasture for such store of muttons

lines.text: If the ground be overcharged, you were best stick her.
lines.plainText: If the ground be overcharged you were best stick her

lines.text: Nay, in that you are astray; 'twere best pound you.
lines.plainText: Nay in that you are astray 'twere best pound you

lines.text: Nay, sir, less than a pound shall serve me for carrying your letter.
lines.plainText: Nay sir less than a pound shall serve me for carrying your letter

lines.text: You mistake; I mean the pound, a pinfold.
lines.plainText: You mistake I mean the pound a pinfold

lines.text: From a pound to a pin? Fold it over and over,
lines.plainText: From a pound to a pin Fold it over and over

lines.text: 'Tis threefold too little for carrying a letter to your lover.
lines.plainText: 'Tis threefold too little for carrying a letter to your lover

lines.text: But what said she?
lines.plainText: But what said she

lines.text: [Nods his head.] Ay.
lines.plainText: Nods his head Ay

lines.text: Nod—"Ay". Why, that's "noddy".
lines.plainText: NodAy Why that's noddy

lines.text: You mistook, sir. I say she did nod, and you ask me if she did nod; and I say "Ay".
lines.plainText: You mistook sir I say she did nod and you ask me if she did nod and I say Ay

lines.text: And that set together is "noddy".
lines.plainText: And that set together is noddy

lines.text: Now you have taken the pains to set it together, take it for your pains.
lines.plainText: Now you have taken the pains to set it together take it for your pains

lines.text: No, no, you shall have it for bearing the letter.
lines.plainText: No no you shall have it for bearing the letter

lines.text: Well, I perceive I must be fain to bear with you.
lines.plainText: Well I perceive I must be fain to bear with you

lines.text: Why, sir, how do you bear with me?
lines.plainText: Why sir how do you bear with me

lines.text: Marry, sir, the letter, very orderly, having nothing but the word "noddy" for my pains.
lines.plainText: Marry sir the letter very orderly having nothing but the word noddy for my pains

lines.text: Beshrew me, but you have a quick wit.
lines.plainText: Beshrew me but you have a quick wit

lines.text: And yet it cannot overtake your slow purse.
lines.plainText: And yet it cannot overtake your slow purse

lines.text: Come, come, open the matter; in brief, what said she?
lines.plainText: Come come open the matter in brief what said she

lines.text: Open your purse, that the money and the matter may be both at once delivered.
lines.plainText: Open your purse that the money and the matter may be both at once delivered

lines.text: [Giving him a coin.] Well, sir, here is for your pains. What said she?
lines.plainText: Giving him a coin Well sir here is for your pains What said she

lines.text: Truly, sir, I think you'll hardly win her.
lines.plainText: Truly sir I think you'll hardly win her

lines.text: Why? Couldst thou perceive so much from her?
lines.plainText: Why Couldst thou perceive so much from her

lines.text: Sir, I could perceive nothing at all from her; no, not so much as a ducat for delivering your letter. And being so hard to me that brought your mind, I fear she'll prove as hard to you in telling your mind. Give her no token but stones, for she's as hard as steel.
lines.plainText: Sir I could perceive nothing at all from her no not so much as a ducat for delivering your letter And being so hard to me that brought your mind I fear she'll prove as hard to you in telling your mind Give her no token but stones for she's as hard as steel

lines.text: What said she, nothing?
lines.plainText: What said she nothing

lines.text: No, not so much as "Take this for thy pains." To testify your bounty, I thank you, you have testerned me; in requital whereof, henceforth carry your letters yourself. And so, sir, I'll commend you to my master.
lines.plainText: No not so much as Take this for thy pains To testify your bounty I thank you you have testerned me in requital whereof henceforth carry your letters yourself And so sir I'll commend you to my master

lines.text: Go, go, begone, to save your ship from wrack,
lines.plainText: Go go begone to save your ship from wrack

lines.text: Which cannot perish having thee aboard,
lines.plainText: Which cannot perish having thee aboard

lines.text: Being destined to a drier death on shore.
lines.plainText: Being destined to a drier death on shore
